references.text: The Lord confirms that Sarah will bear a son to Abraham and sets a time for the fulfillment of the promise.
Sarah bears Isaac to Abraham in his old age, fulfilling God's promise of a son through her.
God names the son Isaac and confirms that He will establish His covenant with him as an everlasting covenant for his descendants.
God repeats the promise to Jacob that kings shall come from his loins, fulfilling the promise that kings of peoples shall come from Sarah.
Paul uses Sarah and Hagar as an allegory for the new and old covenants, identifying Sarah as the mother of the children of the promise.
Isaiah prophesies about kings who will serve God's people, reflecting the promise that kings of peoples shall come from Sarah.
The concretization of the general promise of a great nation and blessing from Abraham to Sarah as the mother of nations.
A direct parallel confirming that kings shall spring from Abraham's lineage, focusing on the father in 17:6 and the mother in 17:16.
A theological connection stating that all the peoples of the earth shall be blessed through the lineage of Abraham/Sarah.
The link between the general promise of blessing for all nations (12:3) and Sarah's specific role in bearing this people (17:16).
A theological parallel between Sarah and Rebekah, both carrying the promise of 'nations' in their wombs.
A theological contrast between the judgment on the woman's childbirth (3:16) and God's gracious promise of blessing and kings through her (17:16).
A typological connection between Sarah as the mother of the promise of a people and Mary as the mother of the Savior, both bearing a son by God's power.
A typological connection between Sarah's miraculous birth of Isaac and Mary's birth of Jesus, both through God's supernatural intervention.
A theological link between God's promise to the barren Sarah (17:16) and the song of praise about God's power to give children (113:9).
